name: indian mashed eggplant
instructions:
A flexible palette-cleanser side that pairs with many indian curries. Pulverized-eggplant + garlic + basic indian spice bloom + tamarind paste + raisins. Not the same thing as Punjabi baingan bharta (see notes) — this is simpler, more of a side than a headliner.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- eggplant
- garlic
- cumin
- coriander
- turmeric
- fennel seeds (or fennel powder)
- olive oil
- ghee
- tamarind paste
- raisins
- salt

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. PULVERIZE THE EGGPLANT + GARLIC in a food processor into a rough pulp — not a smooth paste, but broken down enough to sauté quickly.
2. SAUTÉ WITH SPICES IN GHEE + OLIVE OIL: heat the fat in a pan, bloom the cumin, coriander, turmeric, and fennel briefly, then add the pulverized eggplant.
3. COVER FOR THE FIRST PART to steam/break down the eggplant — the covered start lets the moisture from the raw eggplant do the initial cook.
4. Uncover once the eggplant is softened and the extra moisture has evaporated. Continue sautéing to drive off remaining water and let the spices mix in.
5. Stir in tamarind paste and raisins near the end. Salt to taste.
notes:
=== A FLEXIBLE PALETTE-CLEANSER SIDE, NOT A HEADLINER ===

The point of this recipe: something to eat as a side alongside indian curries that resets the palate between bites of the main dish. Not designed to stand alone as the entree. The mashed-eggplant texture gives you a cool-ish, mild-ish spoonful that softens up whatever heavier curry you're eating alongside.

=== NOT PUNJABI BAINGAN BHARTA — DIFFERENT DISH ===

Deliberately separated from Punjabi baingan bharta. Baingan bharta is a full curry: roasted-and-charred eggplant broken down into an onion + garlic + tomato masala, cooked long enough to develop deep flavors, served as a main. This recipe is much simpler:
- No roasting the eggplant first (see next note).
- No onion, no tomato, no full masala.
- Cooked quickly rather than long-simmered.
- Palette cleanser side, not entree.

If you want proper baingan bharta, look up a Punjabi recipe — this isn't it.

=== ROASTING THE EGGPLANT FIRST PROBABLY HELPS (BUT NOT REQUIRED HERE) ===

Roasting the eggplant (charring the skin over a flame or in the oven until deeply blackened, then peeling and mashing) is the technique that gives baingan bharta its distinctive smoky depth. It would probably help this recipe too — smoke character + eggplant is a strong pairing.

But this recipe is deliberately more flexible / less technique-forward than that. The raw-eggplant-into-food-processor approach lets you make it fast without pre-roasting; the covered-sauté does enough breakdown to get useable eggplant. Reach for roasted eggplant when you have the time and want the smoky version; use raw when you want a fast side.

=== COVERED SAUTÉ FOR THE FIRST PART ===

Raw pulverized eggplant carries a lot of moisture. The covered start traps that moisture and steams the eggplant through — faster than an open sauté would (which would just drive the moisture off before the eggplant softens). Uncover once the eggplant is soft; then the open-pan phase drives off the remaining water and lets the spices mix in.

=== SERVING PAIRING — EGGPLANT WORKS WITH TOMATO/LEGUME INDIAN CURRIES EXCEPT RAJMA ===

There's a consistent pattern in the cookbook's indian curries: EGGPLANT (either this mashed version OR plain baked/sautéed eggplant) pairs well as a side for the TOMATO + LEGUME curries. The eggplant's mild, mash-textured neutrality sits cleanly against the tomato-forward legume bases without competing.

WORKS WELL WITH:
- [[chana-masala]]
- [[chole-masala]]
- [[mediterranean-dal]]

EXCEPTION — [[rajma]]: rajma is the odd one out. Eggplant doesn't fit here — rajma wants [[braised-turnips]] instead. The turnips' denser root-vegetable character pairs better with rajma's kidney-bean + tomato base than the mash-texture of eggplant does. Follow the eggplant → turnip swap for this one specifically.

PLAIN BAKED OR SAUTÉED EGGPLANT ALSO WORKS: you don't need the full indian-mashed version to hit this pairing. Plain roasted eggplant slices, sautéed cubes, or oven-baked halves all cover the same slot. This recipe is the spice-forward / palette-cleanser version; the plainer preparations are simpler and equally valid pairings.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[himachali-chana-madra]]: this side pairs well with it — cross-referenced from that recipe as a secondary. (Different from the untested pureed-eggplant-in-the-base direction still in that recipe's want-to-try.)
- Other indian curries this pairs with broadly (beyond the tomato/legume pattern above): tikka-masala, coconut-mung-bean-curry, indian-saag-curry. Compatible register; the tomato-legume-except-rajma rule above is more specific.
